rounds.t: Alcohol use disorder, psychotherapy, stimulants, and antipsychotic basics

q.s: A man with alcohol use disorder and normal liver function wants a drug to reduce cravings. Which drug fits, and when should it be avoided?

A man taking a drug for alcohol use disorder drinks a beer and develops flushing, nausea, headache and palpitations. How does the drug work?
o: Inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, causing acetaldehyde buildup

q.s: Which complication is associated with chronic alcohol use?
o: Thiamine deficiency, pancreatitis and peripheral neuropathy

e: Correct. Treatment-resistant and persistent suicidality ("cloze to the edge").

q.s: Atypical antipsychotics treat which symptoms better than typical ones?

e: Correct. "Hal tries pie to fly high."

o: Bipolar disorder with psychosis, Tourette syndrome, OCD and Huntington disease

q.s: Why are antipsychotics slow to be removed from the body?
o: They are lipid soluble and stored in body fat

rounds.t: Antipsychotic adverse effects, lithium, and buspirone

q.s: A woman on risperidone has milky nipple discharge and missed periods. Which pathway is affected?
o: D2 blockade in the tuberoinfundibular pathway, raising prolactin

Two weeks after starting haloperidol, a man cannot sit still, constantly paces and feels inner restlessness. What is the treatment?
e: Correct. Akathisia; benzodiazepines or benztropine also.

q.s: After 6 years of fluphenazine, a woman has repetitive lip smacking, tongue thrusting and grimacing. Which drug treats this?
A patient on haloperidol for 3 weeks develops slow movements, shuffling gait and cogwheel rigidity. What is the treatment?

o: Extrapyramidal symptoms: acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia

q.s: Which cardiac adverse effect is shared by antipsychotics?

o: Agonizing central M1/M4 receptors, while trospium blocks peripheral muscarinic effects

o: Takes 1–2 weeks to work and causes no sedation, addiction or tolerance

q.s: The LiTHIUM mnemonic for lithium adverse effects includes:
o: Low Thyroid, Heart (Ebstein), Insipidus (nephrogenic DI), Unwanted Movements (tremor)

o: Depression, GAD, panic, OCD, PTSD, bulimia and premenstrual dysphoric disorder

q.s: A man with depression and painful diabetic neuropathy wants one drug for both. Which is best?
e: Correct. SNRI also used for fibromyalgia.

An 80-year-old started on amitriptyline becomes confused, constipated, has urinary retention and falls when standing. Which TCA would be better tolerated?
e: Correct. Secondary amines have fewer anticholinergic effects.

q.s: Which TCA is used for OCD?
TCAs cause arrhythmia by blocking which channel?
e: Correct. Widened QRS; treat with NaHCO3.

A smoker with depression wants an antidepressant that will not cause sexual dysfunction or weight gain and may help him quit. Which drug fits?
e: Correct. NE and DA reuptake inhibitor.

q.s: Bupropion is contraindicated in which patients?
o: Those with bulimia or anorexia nervosa

An opioid-dependent man takes sublingual buprenorphine 2 hours after using heroin and quickly develops yawning, sweating and diarrhea. Why?
o: As a partial agonist, buprenorphine displaces heroin and precipitates withdrawal

q.s: A man who completed opioid detoxification wants a long-acting oral drug to prevent relapse. Which fits?
e: Correct. "The long trex back to sobriety."

q.s: Injection drug use increases the risk of which infections?
o: HBV, HCV, HIV, skin infections and right-sided endocarditis
